description:
Blind-spot `2026-05-05-003357` documented that
`benchbox/core/write_primitives/catalog/operations.yaml` carries hand-
stamped `verified <tool> at SF=<x>` comments tied to point-in-time
observations (e.g. 60003 / 4314 / 317 bytes for the ClickHouse smoke;
similar numbers for DuckDB). Three durability problems:

1. No regression alarm if observations drift after a tool upgrade.
2. Doc-vs-yaml-bound skew is unguarded
   (`docs/benchmarks/write-primitives-sketch-functions.md` quotes
   "~4.3KB on ClickHouse" while operations.yaml carries `[1500, 8000]`
   bounds -- they can drift independently with no signal).
3. Verification methodology is not codified -- the ad-hoc SQL script
   that captured the observations lived only in the session that wrote
   them.

This TODO ships a checked-in companion smoke + a doc-yaml consistency
test, and sweeps existing comments for staleness.

anti_patterns.dont: make the smoke run in CI on every PR
anti_patterns.why: it pulls fixtures and runs persist+merge cycles. It is an on-demand sweep tool, run quarterly or when bounds are touched.

anti_patterns.dont: replace the catalog `verified` comments with structured YAML annotations
anti_patterns.why: the comments are reviewer-friendly prose; the smoke + test are the enforcement layer.

preserves.behavior: Doc prose around storage-size claims continues to read naturally; the consistency test parses the existing prose pattern, not a machine-readable annotation.
Existing `expected_value_min/max` bounds in `operations.yaml` are not loosened to make a stale comment pass -- if the smoke shows drift, the bound moves WITH a new dated comment line, not silently.
Existing chDB or other in-flight sketch work is not blocked by this TODO -- the consistency test fails only on declared (yaml-bounded + doc-claimed) ops.

verifications.description: Doc-yaml consistency test exists and passes

work_units.notes:
Grep `benchbox/core/write_primitives/catalog/operations.yaml` for
`verified` and produce a table: comment | tool | tool version at
write time | current tool version | bound | observed bytes today
(if measurable). Any row where current observation is outside the
bound or where the tool version has moved is a sweep finding --
record the table as a checked-in handoff at
`_project/handoffs/catalog-verified-comment-sweep-2026-05-05.md`
(or current date) so a reviewer can diff the next sweep against
it.
work_units.summary: Sweep existing `verified <tool>` comments for date-staleness or version drift

work_units.notes:
Run the persist+merge cycles against the bundled SF=0.01 fixtures
for each tool (DuckDB, ClickHouse-local, optionally chDB) and
print observed bytes per op in a stable format (TSV: tool /
op_id / observed_bytes). Stash it under
`scripts/sketch_storage_smoke.sh` so the next person who refreshes
the numbers has a single command.
work_units.summary: Write `scripts/sketch_storage_smoke.sh` (or `make` target) that prints observed bytes

work_units.notes:
Fast-marked test in `tests/unit/core/write_primitives/
test_doc_yaml_consistency.py` that parses
`docs/benchmarks/write-primitives-sketch-functions.md` for "~Xkb
on <tool>" claims and asserts each falls inside the matching
`operations.yaml` `expected_value_min/max` bound. If the doc claim
is missing a tool the catalog covers, fail with a clear "claim
missing" message. If the bound is missing, fail with "doc claim
has no yaml bound."

Use the smoke output from w2 to refresh the comments. If a bound
legitimately moved (tool upgrade, schema change), document the
bound update with a date + observed-bytes line under the existing
`verified` comment so the next sweep can diff against it.
work_units.summary: Re-stamp any out-of-date catalog comments uncovered by w1

work_units.notes:
Extend `.claude/skills/code/references/five-axis-review.md` with a
sub-axis under Correctness: "For changes that update empirically-
observed numbers in catalog comments or docs, require a checked-in
smoke (or make target) that re-produces the observation, and a
consistency test that fails when doc claims drift outside catalog
bounds." This sub-axis is explicitly delegated to this TODO by
`extend-five-axis-review-rubric` (see its `deferred:` block) so
there is no double-edit risk. The `deps.needs` link below ensures
the parent TODO's six branches land first.
work_units.summary: Add 'durability of empirical claims' sub-axis to the review framework
